headline: product-catalog intermittently rejects GetProduct calls (productCatalogFailure flag), cascading HTTP 500s into cart, recommendations, product pages, and checkout via frontend. Bursts tapered sharply 09:07-09:57 UTC, but all real traffic (and thus the only way to test the flag) went dark at 09:57 -- recovery looks likely, not confirmed.
blast_radius: During active bursts (peak 07:56-08:20 UTC): ~47% of checkout attempts failed, ~38-47% of product detail page loads failed across all 10 catalog product IDs, recommendations failed at a comparable rate. Cart, product browsing, and purchasing were all degraded because every one of those routes calls product-catalog's GetProduct to hydrate data. As of 09:57 UTC, real traffic to the entire storefront (frontend-proxy, frontend, product-catalog, cart, checkout) has stopped completely due to a separate load-generator outage (see inc-002), so current blast radius cannot be measured directly -- only a single manual probe exists as evidence (see revision below).
reasoning: Single causal thread (product-catalog's checkProductFailure gate on the productCatalogFailure flag, code-verified) explains every symptom across every affected route -- one incident, not several, per 'one bad change, many symptoms' heuristic.

revisions.previously_believed: Status open at sev2: heavy failure 07:56-08:20 UTC, tapering bursts, most recent burst 08:50 UTC, too recent (~7 min old at write time) to count as recovery given the established bursty on/off pattern.
revisions.new_evidence: This run's alert alt-001 (log-triage, investigated ~10:53-11:08 UTC) independently re-measured frontend's GetProduct error-count-by-10min-bucket across 07:57-09:57 UTC: 8038(08:57)->8439(+401,09:07)->8487(+48,09:17)->8643(+156,09:27)->8736(+93,09:37)->8804(+68,09:47)->8804(+0,09:57) -- a genuine, monotonically-decelerating error trend, the first real tapering evidence beyond 'no new burst yet.' HOWEVER, success-count growth (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) stopped at the exact same 09:57 timestamp -- because a wholly separate fault (inc-002: load-generator traffic paused) killed ALL real traffic to the storefront at that instant, not because the productCatalogFailure fault cleared. Since then the only evidence is one manual direct probe (GET /api/products/0PUK6V6EV0 at ~10:58 UTC) which returned 200 and incremented product-catalog's GetProduct OK counter by exactly 1, with no Internal error -- a real, first-hand data point, but a single request against a flag whose original code-verified behavior is a per-request, per-product_id targeted evaluation (not a global on/off), so one success cannot rule out the fault still triggering on some fraction of requests or other product IDs.
revisions.now_believes: The fault very likely has subsided (real tapering trend, not mere silence) but this cannot be confirmed at any meaningful sample size because the only traffic source in this environment is currently dark (inc-002) -- the traffic blackout is actively blocking verification of this incident's recovery, which is itself worth flagging rather than papering over. Downgrading sev2->sev3 to reflect that no currently-active harm is being measured (last confirmed burst tapered to zero net growth), while keeping status at 'monitoring' rather than 'resolved' because this is inferred from an evidence gap, not from positive proof of recovery -- resolving on this would violate 'never resolve because an alert stopped firing.'
revisions.why_changed: New, independently-gathered metric evidence (this run's alt-001) plus the discovery that traffic itself stopped for an unrelated reason at the identical timestamp -- both change what can honestly be claimed about current state without changing the underlying root cause, which remains verified.

revisions.previously_believed: n/a -- correcting an alternative hypothesis raised in alt-001, not a prior belief of this incident.
revisions.new_evidence: alt-001 (log-triage, this run) hypothesized the 07:27-08:57 error spike might instead be a transport-level failure from the load-generator's own container restart/draining (~07:19-07:22 UTC), based on Loki showing zero application-level error logs in product-catalog/checkout during the spike.
revisions.now_believes: That Loki-silence observation does not actually contradict this incident's already-verified root cause: checkProductFailure returns a gRPC Internal status directly, before ever reaching getProductFromDB or any app-level error logging -- so Loki silence is exactly what the already-confirmed flag-based mechanism predicts, not evidence of a separate transport-level cause. Treating alt-001's error-spike evidence as corroboration of this incident, not grounds for a competing explanation or a second incident.
revisions.why_changed: Re-examined alt-001's own disconfirming checks against the code-verified RCA already on file for this incident (src/product-catalog/main.go:373-380, gh-verified) and found no actual conflict once the mechanism is accounted for.

rca.root_cause: product-catalog's GetProduct gRPC handler is gated by checkProductFailure, which evaluates the OpenFeature/flagd boolean flag productCatalogFailure (default false, generated binding flags.ProductCatalogFailure) per-request via a targetless evaluation context keyed on product_id. When the flag evaluates true for a given request, GetProduct returns before ever calling getProductFromDB, setting a gRPC error with code Internal (13) and the literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled' -- exactly matching the trace evidence (rpc.grpc.status_code=13, grpc.error_message text) verbatim. Because nearly every user-facing route (product detail, cart, recommendations, checkout) calls GetProduct to hydrate product data, this single upstream fault cascades into HTTP 500s across all of them, which is exactly the blast radius alert-grouping observed. This is the demo's deliberate fault-injection code path executing correctly as designed when the flag is on for a given evaluation, not an accidental bug in the flag-check logic itself -- the bursty on/off pattern reflects the flag being toggled/cycled by the fault scenario, not a malfunction in checkProductFailure.
rca.verify_detail: A second, fresh sub-agent, given only the bare claim (file src/product-catalog/main.go, function checkProductFailure, called from GetProduct, gRPC code Internal, literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', returned before the DB lookup) and no prior reasoning, independently confirmed via `gh api repos/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/contents/src/product-catalog` that the file exists at that path, then fetched the real raw content and quoted: GetProduct calling checkProductFailure at line 373; checkProductFailure at lines 419-420 evaluating flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value(ctx, openfeature.NewTargetlessEvaluationContext(map[string]any{"product_id": id})); and the error branch at lines 374-377 returning status.Error(codes.Internal, msg) with msg == 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', with getProductFromDB only reached afterward at line 380. Verdict: CONFIRMED -- every specific element of the claim (path, function, caller, flag reference, error code, exact message, ordering relative to the DB call) is directly and verbatim supported by the real file content, not a plausible-sounding guess.

escalation.observed: Real error-rate tapering to zero net growth (09:07-09:57 UTC) immediately followed by total traffic blackout at the same instant (inc-002), leaving zero real-traffic evidence of whether the productCatalogFailure fault has actually cleared.
escalation.ruled_out: Resolution cannot be claimed from the current quiet period alone -- the quiet is fully explained by an unrelated traffic outage, not by confirmed absence of the fault; one manual probe succeeded but is too small a sample given the flag's per-request targeted evaluation.
escalation.open_question: Once inc-002's load-generator traffic resumes (or root-cause-analysis runs enough repeated manual probes across multiple product IDs), check whether productCatalogFailure-pattern errors (gRPC Internal, exact message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled') recur at any rate -- that is the only evidence that would actually confirm or reopen this incident at full severity.

remediation.second_opinion: PASS. "A narrow, correctly-scoped, non-destructive change: it improves error semantics for a genuinely transient, intentionally-injected failure, leaves the fault-injection mechanism fully intact, and doesn't remove, weaken, or hide anything." Noted limitation: does not by itself reduce blast radius absent caller-side retry logic on the calling services -- flagged as necessary follow-up work, not a blocker.
remediation.summary: Reclassified product-catalog GetProduct's flag-triggered failure from gRPC codes.Internal to codes.Unavailable (main.go:377) -- correct error semantics per grpc-go's own doc comments for an intentionally transient, flag-simulated failure; the flag and fault-injection mechanism itself are untouched.

release_approval.own_re_review: Independent re-fetch of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/main/src/product-catalog/main.go (not trusted from remediation's copy) confirmed: (1) GetProduct at the claimed location currently reads exactly `return nil, status.Error(codes.Internal, msg)` inside the `if p.checkProductFailure(ctx, req.Id)` branch -- the diff's context and removed line match the real file verbatim; (2) checkProductFailure (lines 419-420) and the flags.ProductCatalogFailure evaluation are untouched by the proposal -- fault-injection mechanism fully intact, independently re-derived rather than trusted from the RCA's earlier verify; (3) diff is minimal and scoped: one functional line changed (Internal->Unavailable) plus an explanatory comment, no other lines, no unrelated files touched (PR only adds sre-engineer/remediations/incident-001/proposed-fix.diff and rationale.md documenting a proposal against the upstream demo repo, consistent with this project's read-only constraint on open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo -- the change is not applied to any real running system by this merge); (4) no reckless pattern -- no error swallowed (still returns an error), no check removed, nothing hardcoded, and the error message text is unchanged so any log/trace-based detection keyed on that string is preserved, meaning this does not make a future incident harder to detect; (5) codes.Unavailable is a valid, already-imported identifier in google.golang.org/grpc/codes (same package as codes.Internal, already in use elsewhere in this file for SearchProducts) -- syntactically valid Go. All four release-approval checks hold independently.
